calls.reason: Slack AI's $10 add-on price and Zylo's note on cautious buying back up parts of the claim. But 'underwhelming' and 'commoditized' are value judgments, and Computerworld reports cheaper options and possible benefits.
The Agentforce pricing announcement shows a SaaS vendor selling AI. Apple's consumer AI launch points to other drivers. Nothing in the packet measures which cause dominated across the industry.
Bain says AI compute runs about 1-3x hosting costs and is falling, and Anthropic reports caching cuts costs. That is mixed on 'multitudes higher', and no matched comparison shows costs rising.
The Workday and Box announcements show generic drafting features, and ChatGPT's free tier covers writing tasks. But a few examples cannot show that nearly all products include such features.

The only evidence is Salesforce's own announcement, which describes planning and automation features. There is no independent comparison with earlier chatbots to show either equivalence or a real difference.

Figma's CFO said the cost of serving AI features hurt gross margin in Q3 2025. Its non-GAAP gross margin fell from 92% to 86%. That fits the low 'begin to eat into' bar, though only one company is documented.
